Over time, routine pallet movement inevitably leads to structural wear and tear on pallet racking systems throughout facilities in Trafford Park Industrial Estate, Westbrook Park and Centurion Park.

During comprehensive SEMA-approved racking safety inspections conducted in Trafford Park, our qualified inspectors routinely discover localized structural damage concentrated at lower upright levels. In high-density pallet racking configurations typical of Trafford Park Industrial Estate, Westbrook Park and Centurion Park, unshielded forklift impacts to front upright columns, bent diagonal bracing, dislodged safety beam locks, twisted steel footplates, and floor anchor bolt shearing are among the most frequently identified hazards. In cold storage and food production facilities across Trafford Park, ambient moisture accumulation and washdown procedures often accelerate localized steel corrosion and frame fatigue. Furthermore, rapid stock rotation frequently leads to unrecorded rack beam alterations, missing beam safety pins, overloaded beam levels, and reduced aisle clearances. Regular professional racking inspections across Trafford Park ensure that structural defects are identified early, categorized accurately under SEMA green, amber, and red risk standards, and rectified promptly before catastrophic failure occurs, ensuring complete health and safety compliance.

faqs.q: How often should racking be inspected in Trafford Park?
faqs.a: In Trafford Park, heavy-duty racking systems should undergo a formal inspection by a competent SEMA-approved inspector at least once every 12 months in full compliance with Health and Safety Executive guidelines (HSG76). However, for busy distribution hubs in areas like Trafford Park Industrial Estate, Westbrook Park and Centurion Park experiencing continuous forklift traffic and multi-shift operations, semi-annual or quarterly expert inspections are strongly recommended. In addition to annual external audits, warehouse management must conduct internal weekly visual checks to identify immediate hazards such as severe column impacts, loose beam safety clips, or dislodged safety pins.

faqs.q: What does a racking inspection cover in Trafford Park?
faqs.a: A comprehensive racking inspection in Trafford Park covers an end-to-end structural assessment of all pallet racking, cantilever systems, drive-in racking, and mezzanine storage structures across your facility. Our SEMA-approved inspector thoroughly checks upright columns for impact deformation, verifies beam deflective tolerances, inspects diagonal bracing for twists or cracks, checks floor fixings and footplates for anchor shear, and confirms the presence of beam safety locks. We also evaluate rack loading notices, beam height configurations, pallet condition, and overall aisle clearances to ensure complete workplace safety compliance.

faqs.q: Is racking inspection a legal requirement in Trafford Park?
faqs.a: Yes, maintaining safe racking in Trafford Park is a legal requirement governed by the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER Regulation 6) and the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974. The HSE explicitly references the HSG76 guide (Warehousing and Storage: A guide to health and safety) which dictates that storage racking must be inspected regularly by a qualified expert. Non-compliance can result in substantial HSE prohibition notices, severe fines, or corporate liability prosecutions in the event of an avoidable collapse or injury.

faqs.q: What happens after a racking inspection in Trafford Park?
faqs.a: Following the completion of a racking inspection in Trafford Park, you will receive a comprehensive written report detailing every identified defect categorized using the standard SEMA color-coded risk scale (Green, Amber, Red). Red Risk items represent immediate danger and require instant offloading and isolation; Amber Risk items need action within 4 weeks; and Green Risk items require ongoing monitoring. The report includes high-resolution photography, clear layout diagrams, component replacement advice, and an official Certificate of Inspection to satisfy insurers and HSE auditors.
